newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coles Myer says break up in background.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coles Myer says break up in background.

text.p: Coles Myer Ltd chief executive Dennis Eck said on Sunday a break up of the retailer, Australia's biggest, was likely to always shadow the company but it was not considering it at the moment.

Asked in a television interview if the break up plan first raised in 1995 by former executive chairman Solomon Lew was behind the company, Eck said: "I think if I were to say that, that wouldn't be true.

"I think ultimately the test for the shareholder has always got to be can I create more value for somebody holding my share and running with it, or is more value created by unlocking it in some other way.

"I think you would expect us always to have that as the bogey in the background ... it will always be there but right now we're so busy trying to unlock the value that we see that it's not something that's occupying our attention ...," Eck told the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme.
Eck also said Coles Myer had no immediate plans for a share buy-back, saying more capital needed to be spent refurbishing its Kmart discount variety stores and Myer Grace Bros department stores.
"I don't rule out any options ever, but just to restate it, we're comfortable with our ability to effectively deploy our assets in the short and mid-term," Eck said.
Coles Myer last week reported a stronger-than-expected net profit of A$273.6 million for the half-year ended January 26, against A$194.5 million a year earlier.
